newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary coalition party chief quits.
newsitem.headline: Hungary coalition party chief quits.

text.p: Ivan Peto, president and parliamentary leader of the junior partner in Hungary's coalition government, resigned unexpectedly on Monday.

Under fire in a scandal springing from post-communist privatisation, Peto had offered to quit last year but party leaders in the Alliance of Free Democrats talked him out of it. This time they accepted.
The party holds almost a fifth of the seats in parliament but Prime Minister Gyula Horn's Socialist Party has a majority without it.
Horn told reporters he was sorry about Peto's resignation but "I don't think this should affect or weaken coalition co-operation."
Peto announced his resignation to his party's national executive but gave no reason. He was expected to make a statement later on Monday.
According to a party source, his departure appeared to be linked to the privatisation scandal, which involved unexplained payments of $5 million to a consultant hired to negotiate land deals in 1996.
Some of the money is alleged to have reached a businessman close to the Free Democrats and Peto has been criticised by opponents for not taking responsibility in the affair.

The Free Democrats' representatives in the cabinet include Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze, who will fill in as party leader, and Istvan Szent-Ivanyi, a junior foreign minister who becomes acting parliamentary leader.
